transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t stop noticing this sagging, uneven area around my jaw and neck. Other people tell me it looks normal, but I feel like it’s the first thing people notice—families, nurses, people at church.
When others tell you it looks normal, can you consider that they might be right, or are you completely certain the flaw is there?
I mean, I hear them, but I don’t really believe it. When I look at my jaw and neck, I see the sagging and unevenness right away. It feels like that’s what people notice first when they look at me.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time doing things like checking mirrors, adjusting your clothes to hide your neck, or touching the area repeatedly?

Yes. Before work or a meeting, I keep going back to the bathroom mirror to fix my collar and hair around my neck. Then I’ll check my phone camera again. Sometimes I ask my daughter if it looks strange. It’s made me late more than once.
Do you view this sagging as purely a cosmetic flaw, or are you worried it might be a sign of an underlying medical illness?
I’m not really thinking it’s an illness. It just looks wrong to me—like it’s sagging more than it should—and I want to hide it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits excessive preoccupation with a perceived physical defect (sagging and uneven jaw and neck) that appears normal to others, accompanied by compulsive checking, camouflaging behaviors, and reassurance seeking that result in functional impairment (lateness). In ICD-10, Body Dysmorphic Disorder (dysmorphophobia) is categorized under F45.2 (Hypochondriacal disorder).

confirmed_symptoms: Preoccupation with a perceived defect in physical appearance (sagging, unevenness of jaw/neck) that is not observable to others
Belief that the perceived defect is prominently noticed by others despite reassurance
Camouflaging behaviors (adjusting clothes and hair to conceal the neck)

additional_requirements: Absence of fear of underlying systemic medical disease (purely cosmetic concern)
